    The mesh category k(Γ_A) and standardness #

    graded-category.tex: for Q = Γ_A, choose bases in the one-dimensional irreducible spaces. The first and second maps of the almost split sequence ending at a nonprojective Y have components u_a (σ a) and v_a a modulo J², with u_a, v_a ≠ 0; the mesh relation is r_Y = ∑_{a : X → Y} c_{Y,a} (σ a) a with c_{Y,a} = u_a v_a (eq:scalar-mesh), and k(Γ_A) = C(Γ_A, c). Definition 1.2 (def:standardness): A is standard if there is a k-linear equivalence k(Γ_A) ≃ ind(mod A) sending each vertex to its labelled module.

    Formalization:

    • Γ_A is the translation quiver arTranslationQuiver of ARTranslationQuiver.lean; by Lemma 2.2 (SquareFree.lean) it has at most one arrow between ordered vertices.
    • An ArrowBases value chooses a basis of each Irr(x, y), indexed by the arrows x → y.
    • The almost split sequence ending at a nonprojective x is the canonical one of the vendored Auslander--Reiten library, with its chosen decomposition of the middle term. For an arrow a : y → x, the summands isomorphic to y are the occurrences of y; there is exactly one, because their number is dim Irr(y, x) = 1. The coefficient is c_{x,a} = ∑_{occurrences i of y} u_i v_i, where u_i and v_i are the coordinates, in the chosen bases, of the classes of the components τx → y and y → x at i. It is nonzero because the components are irreducible, so their classes in the one-dimensional spaces Irr are nonzero.
    • k(Γ_A) is the scalar mesh category C(Γ_A, c) of Definition 2.4.

    The manuscript shows that a different choice of bases or almost split sequences changes k(Γ_A) only by an object-fixing isomorphism (graded-category.tex); Definition 1.2 is formalized with an existential choice of bases.
